paragraphs: Five timer reload words, indexed by the Speed Booster counter times two.
The first word also initializes the adjacent timer/counter pair: its low
byte is the initial delay and its high byte is the starting counter.
Later reloads are ORed into the low timer byte while preserving the counter.
Initial jump velocities for air, water, and lava/acid, in that order.
The integer and fractional components live in parallel speed/subspeed
tables. !SPF scales the velocity for the selected regional frame rate.
Each movement type selects a 12-byte row: acceleration, maximum speed,
then deceleration. Each value occupies two words; wordSwap places the
integer word before the fractional word consumed by the movement code.
SetTimer takes packed BCD minutes and seconds ($MMSS), not binary seconds.
Clear the old countdown before loading the duration and startup state.
SetTimer takes packed BCD minutes and seconds ($MMSS), not binary seconds.
Startup begins with an initial delay before the timer display moves into place.
Fuse countdown loaded for newly fired bombs before their explosion sequence.
regional selects the NTSC or PAL reload value.
Item messages wait for lag frames before accepting input. The collecting
PLM schedules the music-resume delay separately from this message wait.
The regular Zoomer shares its movement state machine with other crawlers.
InitAI_Zoomer_MZoomer chooses its starting orientation; MainAI_Crawlers
dispatches the handler installed by the orientation's animation script.
X is the enemy slot and Y points to the script's next word: a bank $A3
movement-handler address. Consume that word and return Y to the interpreter.
Zoomer/Zeela orientation lists install the handler before their first frame.
Their frame loops skip this command, so they do not overwrite a falling
handler on every animation cycle.
Before initialisation, Enemy.instList holds the population's initialisation
value, not a script pointer. Its low two bits select upside right, left,
down or up (0..3). Replace that value with the matching instruction list,
then fall through to the shared initialiser with X still the enemy slot.
Start with no visible spritemap and a do-nothing handler. An instruction
timer of one lets the orientation script install both on its next update.
Enemy.init0 selects the speed-table word copied into both velocity fields;
$00FF skips the lookup; existing velocities still pass through sign selection.
Crawling velocities are signed 8.8 pixels per frame, unlike the separate
integer/fractional word pair used while falling.
The low two property bits choose the initial velocity signs independently
of the script-orientation value: 0 negates X, 2 negates Y, 1 and 3 leave
both unchanged. These signs are also applied when the speed lookup was skipped.
These four orientation tables use Enemy.init1 directly as a byte offset
(0, 2, 4, 6, 8 or $0A), not an element number. It selects the species' script.
A corner turn chooses a new orientation list and resets the instruction timer
to one; that list installs the corresponding horizontal or vertical handler.
Crawler.function is a bank-local handler address, not a numeric state ID.
Tail-jump with X = EnemyIndex; the selected handler returns with RTL to
the AI caller. Orientation scripts and falling transitions share this field.
On a wall, X velocity presses into the surface and Y velocity moves along it.
A type $0014 earthquake at timer $001E saves this handler and selects falling.
That change does not return early: this invocation still performs its crawl step.
Convert signed 8.8 velocity to the movement helpers' signed 16.16 distance:
clear $12/$14, sign-extend, then store the velocity across $13/$14.
Add one pixel in the X direction to probe wall contact before travelling
along Y. The helpers return carry set on collision; $14.$12 is scratch
for the current move, not a persistent X- or Y-specific variable.
The wall probe collided, but travel along Y hit an inside corner.
Reverse X velocity and choose a floor/ceiling animation from the Y sign.
Restarting that script switches movement to the horizontal handler.
No wall contact: count this unsupported turn. Four consecutive misses
save the current handler and select falling instead of turning again.
Earlier misses reverse Y and select a floor/ceiling script to follow
the outside corner. Finding wall contact resets the shared turn counter.
Falling uses a separate signed 16.16 Y velocity: $14 receives the integer
word and $12 the fractional word. Move first, then accelerate if unobstructed.
A collision restores nonFallingFunction after clearing fall speed and the
turn counter. For the $00FF speed-lookup sentinel, landing first assigns
$0080 (0.5 pixels per frame) to both crawling velocities.
Add $8000 to the fractional word in NTSC, or $A000 in PAL, propagating
carry into the integer word. Acceleration stops once the integer part
is at least four; this test does not clamp an existing overshoot.
On a floor or ceiling, Y velocity presses into the surface and X travels
along it. The same earthquake trigger as vertical crawling saves this
handler and selects falling without skipping the current crawl step.
Expand signed 8.8 Y velocity into $14.$12, then add one pixel in its
direction to probe floor/ceiling contact. With support, calculate the
slope-adjusted X distance and move along the surface. A clear X move
is followed by vertical alignment to a non-square slope.
The support probe collided, but X travel hit an inside corner.
Reverse Y velocity and use the X sign to select a wall-facing script.
Its initial command installs the vertical movement handler.
No floor/ceiling contact: share the vertical handler's unsupported-turn
counter. On the fourth miss save this handler and fall; otherwise reverse
X and select a wall-facing script to follow the outside corner.
Finding support resets the counter before attempting X travel.
Input X is the enemy slot. Sample the supporting edge selected by the sign
of Y velocity. A slope block with BTS subtype >= 5 selects an 8.8 multiplier;
multiply the magnitude of the 8.8 X velocity and restore its sign.
Return the 16.16 move distance in $14.$12 with X restored to EnemyIndex.
Without such a slope, just expand the original velocity to 16.16.
The stored Crawler.XVelocity is not changed by this adjustment.
InitAI_Waver splits the regional horizontal speed and chooses its direction.
MainAI_Waver moves horizontally, derives vertical distance from a wave phase,
and coordinates steady/spinning animation scripts through a completion flag.
Population parameter 1 bit 0 selects left (0) or right (1), not a speed index.
The animation index packs facing in bit 0 and spinning in bit 1.
Indices 0/1 select steady-left/right; 2/3 select spinning-left/right.
newInstListIndex requests a state; instListIndex caches the installed list.
Both spin scripts execute this after their four eight-tick frames.
Signal main AI through spinFinishedFlag; do not change facing or velocity.
There is no parameter word to consume. The following sleep holds the last
spin frame until main AI clears the spin bit and selects a steady list.
The regional 8.8 speed is $0180 (NTSC) or $01D0 (PAL), split into
a signed integer word and a fractional word for 16.16 movement.
Parameter 1 bit 0 set keeps positive X motion; clear negates the full
8.8 value before splitting it. The .facingLeft name marks the common
tail, not the direction of the branch that reaches it.
Seed the steady-left list directly, then request index 0/1 from the same bit.
The animation helper only resets timers when that requested index changes.
Move in X first. On a wall hit, reconstruct the original 8.8 speed from
overlapping velocity bytes, negate it, and toggle facing while clearing spin.
That path skips Y movement and phase advance but still checks animation.
Without an X collision, use the shared negative-sine helper's integer return
as a Y distance; this is phase-driven velocity, not an absolute Y coordinate.
Y collision reflects the phase; otherwise advance it by two before testing spin.
Pass radius 4 and the low-byte phase to the shared negative-sine helper.
Only its signed integer return is used; $12 is zero, so the fractional
sine result is discarded rather than accumulated as vertical subpixels.
A blocked Y move adds $80 and masks to a byte, selecting the opposite
vertical phase instead of taking the normal +2 advance.
Advance the phase only after both X and Y movement report no collision.
The stored word is not masked here: the sine helper uses its low byte,
and the animation test uses its low seven bits. A wall leaves it unchanged.
The low-seven-bit phase test requests spinning at $38 and $B8.
Keep facing in bit 0 and set spin in bit 1. Repeating the same request
does not restart its script because SetWaverInstList compares cached indices.
This check also runs after either collision path, not only after free movement.
Consume the flag set by the spin script after all four frames.
Clear only the spin bit in the requested index, preserving its current
facing, then select the matching steady list. The flag is cleared once.
Switch scripts only when the desired index differs from the installed index.
An unchanged index returns without resetting animation timing, allowing the
spin's frames to finish. On a change, resolve the two-byte table entry,
set instruction timer 1, and clear the previous script's loop counter.
The reset vector enters in emulation mode. Switch to native mode and the
bank-$80 FastROM mirror, establish the stack and direct page, then initialise
low RAM and the display. Upload the SPC engine before joining CommonBootSection.
The polling delay below is retained as written; its original purpose is unknown.
Cold boot and SoftReset converge here. Force blank, clear bank $7E and initialise
CPU/PPU shadows, sound queues and sprite-transfer state before enabling NMI.
Finish the SRAM/demo checks, then jump to MainGameLoop without a return address.
NMI may run before the first frame request; its no-request path skips uploads.
Prepare one game-state iteration, then publish it through WaitForNMI.
Music/HDMA logic and the random seed advance before the state handler; sound
queues and RAM OAM are finalised afterwards. The state-specific handlers choose
which simulation systems run; this loop is also used by menus and cinematics.
The low state byte indexes 45 bank-local word pointers ($00..$2C), with no bounds
check. A state change inside a handler affects the next dispatch, not this call.
Set NMI_Request only after the caller's frame buffers and transfer queues are
ready. NMI clears it after uploads and controller sampling, releasing this
busy-wait. An NMI with no request takes the lag path instead of consuming
partially prepared data. NMI must be enabled or this routine cannot finish.
Processor flags and the data bank are restored; A is used by the polling loop
and byte-index mode truncates the high bytes of X and Y.
Set bit 7 in both $4200 and its shared DP_IRQAutoJoy shadow. Preserve the
h/v-counter interrupt and auto-joypad bits. This is separate from CLI/SEI:
the CPU's IRQ-disable flag does not enable or disable NMI.
Clear bit 7 in both $4200 and DP_IRQAutoJoy, preserving the other control bits.
Keeping the shadow in sync matters because Update_IO_Registers uploads it again.
A subsequent WaitForNMI requires NMI to be re-enabled.
The native NMI vector enters through bank $00; jump to the bank-$80 mirror,
save full-width registers and establish direct page $0000 before doing work.
A nonzero NMI_Request gates the prepared-frame transfers and input sampling.
Servicing it clears the request and lag count and advances NMI_8bitFrameCounter
and NMI_FrameCounter. NMI_Counter advances on both serviced and lag paths.
RTI restores the interrupted processor status as well as its program address.
Refresh the table-address registers for six HDMA-object slots. The object index
steps by two; each active slot supplies a DMA-channel offset and a word pointer.
Later, DP_HDMAEnable is written to $420C after the queued VRAM transfers.
No frame is ready. Leave transfer queues and sampled controller state untouched;
increment the byte-sized consecutive lag count and its unsigned high-water mark.
The count wraps at $100; the high-water mark is retained across that wrap.
Rejoin the common exit to count this NMI and restore the interrupted context
without advancing the serviced-frame counters.
Dispatch h/v-counter IRQ commands for scanline effects such as the HUD split
and door-transition drawing. DP_IRQCmd is already a word-table byte offset.
The command returns its successor in A, the next horizontal target in X and
vertical target in Y. Store all three before restoring the interrupted registers.
Unlike NMI, this entry does not change the direct-page base; direct-page command
state uses the engine's existing direct page.
Schedule the title-sequence loader and choose the initial attract-mode demo set.
The count found during boot normally starts at set 0; a count of four selects
set 3. Increment GameState to 1 and return to the outer frame loop.
Run the normal gameplay handler before advancing the fade-in. Actors and room
logic therefore continue while the screen brightens. When the brightness shadow
is exactly $0F, clear the fade timers and increment GameState (normally 7 to 8).
Order the gameplay subsystems, rather than running every entity from one loop.
Select enemy lists first; Samus's current-state phase precedes interactions and
enemy AI, and her new-state phase follows the main enemy routine. Projectiles,
PLMs, tile animation and collision passes run before scrolling and sprite drawing.
Individual handlers still control their own frozen/disabled behavior. The debug
skip below bypasses this simulation block, but not the shared housekeeping tail.
This tail also runs after the debug skip: HUD and background scroll calculations,
room main ASM, energy/game-time handling, shaking and hurt-timer/list cleanup.
The in-game clock is updated by the called helper, not by counting all NMIs.
Return to MainGameLoop for sound processing, OAM finalisation and publication.
Called near the end of a serviced NMI, after the graphics work. Wait until the
auto-joypad busy bit clears before reading the controller result. Derive newly
pressed buttons from current AND (current XOR previous), then maintain held
button repeat state. The no-request NMI path does not call this routine.
Accept a newly pressed Start only in gameplay state $08, outside Ceres, with
no power-bomb flag, frozen-time flag or enemy-pause door-transition flag set.
Prime the brightness fade and select state $0C; do not load the pause menu here.
Gameplay continues while brightness decreases. Test only the low brightness
nibble for zero, then advance to pause graphics setup. This differs from the
unpause menu fade-out, which waits for the full brightness shadow to equal $80.
Replace the gameplay display while dark: suspend HDMA and animated tiles, back
up graphics state, run the room's pause hook, then load menu tilemaps and colors.
PHP/PHB protect the hook caller; PHK plus PEA form a synthetic long return frame.
The indirect JML uses a 24-bit hook pointer. Its RTL consumes that frame before
PLB/PLP restore the separately saved bank and status.
Draw the pause menu while increasing brightness. An exact $0F shadow means
full brightness with forced blank clear; then clear fade timers and advance
to the interactive paused state. No ordinary gameplay handler is called here.
Maintain timed held/new input, the selected pause page, HUD and palette animation.
This uses MainPauseRoutine, not GameState_8_MainGameplay. The outer main loop
still services music/HDMA logic, sound queues, OAM and the NMI frame handshake.
Dispatch the pause menu's own eight-state machine, independently of GameState.
Indices 0 and 1 are the interactive map and equipment pages; 2..4 switch from
map to equipment, and 5..7 switch back. Double the index for bank-local word
pointers. The table has no bounds check; handlers return with RTS, this entry RTL.
Use the pause menu's timed held/new input stream, unlike PauseCheck's new-only
controller input. Start queues confirmation, primes fade-out and flashes the
button label before incrementing GameState, normally $0F to unpausing state $10.
Refresh the L/R/Start tilemap even when no Start input was accepted.
Keep drawing the selected pause page and pressed-Start highlight while fading
out. Wait for exactly $80 (forced blank set, brightness zero), not just a zero
brightness nibble, before advancing to gameplay graphics restoration.
Rebuild the gameplay display before fading it in: restore saved colors and
graphics state, reload gameplay assets, then run the room's long unpause hook.
PHK/PEA build the hook's RTL return frame; the separate saved bank and status
remain on the stack until after HDMA, animated tiles and movement sounds resume.
Advance GameState before restoring the handler's outer saved processor status.
Run gameplay while the restored display brightens. On an exact $0F brightness
shadow, clear fade timers and explicitly select gameplay state $08.
This state resets to $08 instead of advancing to the next numeric game state.
Reload gameplay graphics while interrupts are controlled for direct VRAM work.
Mask IRQs, stop DMA, disable NMI and h/v-counter interrupts, then rebuild CRE,
tileset, background, visible-room and PLM graphics. Re-enable the interrupt
sources and restore the caller's saved bank and processor status before RTL.
Call the bank-$82 preliminary door/elevator phase using a synthetic near return:
PEA pushes .manualReturn-1 and the indirect JMP reaches a phase ending in RTS.
Carry clear keeps state $09; carry set advances the state and tail-calls
GameState_A_LoadingNextRoom immediately in the same outer-loop iteration.
Ordinary doors and elevators with negative direction finish this preliminary
phase immediately with carry set. The other elevator path selects the regional
downward delay and executes its first timer decrement in the same call.
Decrement the regional delay before testing its sign. A resulting zero still
runs enemies and draws the scene with carry clear; only a negative result
returns carry set to release game state $09. This path draws inanimate Samus
rather than calling her ordinary gameplay state handlers.
Prepare the room transition once before entering the phase dispatcher. Set the
transition flags, choose fade target colors while retaining selected HUD/timer
colors, queue the door sound and inhibit further ordinary sound requests.
Select WaitForSoundsToFinish and advance GameState, normally $0A to $0B.
Later phases return to the main frame loop; the room is not loaded in one call.
Dispatch one saved DoorTransitionFunction per call through an indirect near JMP.
PEA supplies the return word minus one expected by the phase's RTS. Phases may
select another data bank; save and restore the caller's bank around dispatch.
After the phase returns, draw an active countdown timer before the common exit.
Keep running enemies and drawing while all three sound-library queues drain.
Each queue is empty when (next index - consumed index) AND $0F is zero.
This checks queued requests, not whether a sound has finished playing on the SPC.
Only after all three rings are empty select the palette fade-out phase.
Fade palette entries toward the targets prepared by state $0A. This is palette
interpolation, not HandleFadingOut's display-brightness fade. While unfinished,
run enemies and draw the scene; on carry set, schedule door-header/HDMA setup.
Load door metadata, remove old HDMA objects and clear their processing-enable
bit. Request scanline IRQ command $08 through DP_NextIRQCmd, allowing the
interrupt chain to adopt it, then schedule camera alignment.
Align the camera axis perpendicular to travel: Y for horizontal doors, X for
vertical doors. Each unfinished call moves that coordinate by one pixel toward
a $100-pixel boundary; low bytes $80..$FF increment, $01..$7F decrement.
The unaligned word load places the coordinate's pixel low byte in A's high byte.
Immediate BIT #$FF00 tests it for zero but preserves the load's N flag for BMI.
Both paths refresh scrolling. A step reaching alignment still returns first;
only an already-aligned entry selects FixDoorsMovingUp.
Select the room-data bank and preserve elevator-related explored-map state
around loading the destination room and state headers. Initialise room effects
and decompress level/scroll/CRE data before scheduling scrolling setup.
This is one phase of state $0B, not the complete destination-room setup.
Wait for all music-queue timer words to clear; this is not a test that the
currently playing track has ended. Once clear, select the Samus-placement
correction phase and request the destination music only if the track changed.
Run destination-room animated tiles, enemies and enemy projectiles while
interpolating colors toward the room's target palette. Draw Samus through the
inanimate path rather than her ordinary state handlers. When the palette helper
returns carry set, restore sound queuing, clear transition flags and select
gameplay state $08. This is distinct from the pause/unpause brightness fades.
Read the fixed eleven-byte room header in bank $8F, then select a room state
from the condition-function stream that follows it. Width and height are stored
in screen units and multiplied by sixteen for block dimensions. The hardware
multiplier uses only each block dimension's low byte; double its word result
to obtain LevelDataSize in bytes. This routine does not decompress level data.
Load the selected state's resource pointers, music, FX, enemy population/set,
layer-2 scroll-control bytes and cached room-main callback. Long pointers are
assembled with overlapping word stores: high word first, then the low word.
The population chooses placements/parameters; the enemy set chooses graphics
and palettes. PLMs, library backgrounds and setup ASM are read by later loaders.
Walk bank-$8F condition functions starting eleven bytes after the room header.
Each function word is followed by that condition's own payload; X points at
the payload when the function runs. PEA supplies an RTS return to the loop.
A failed condition advances X past its payload and returns with RTS. A match
jumps to Use_StatePointer_inX, which drops that near return and exits with RTL.
X is the chosen state-header address, not the address of a pointer to dereference.
The default condition reaches this routine with X immediately after its own
function word, at the inline default state header. Matching non-default checks
instead load X from their payload's state pointer. Discard the scan loop's
two-byte return before RTL returns to the selector's long caller.
This condition's payload is one event byte followed by a two-byte state pointer.
On success select that pointed-to state through the common long-return exit.
On failure skip all three payload bytes and RTS back to the condition scan.
Read the optional PLM list from state offset $14. Six-byte records contain a
PLM ID, X/Y block bytes and argument word; a zero ID terminates the list.
Attempt each spawn without checking its carry result, then execute door ASM
and room setup ASM in that order, even when the PLM list was absent or empty.
Finally set ElevatorStatus to 2 only when the door's elevator property is set.
State offset $18 is an optional bank-$8F setup callback. A zero word skips it;
otherwise JSR invokes the setup routine, which returns with RTS. Restore the
saved data bank and processor status before RTL returns to the long caller.
This wrapper expects the state-header data to be readable in the entry data bank.
Read the optional door-ASM word from bank-$83 door data, but execute it in
bank $8F. For a nonzero pointer, PEA builds the callback's near RTS return
before the indirect JMP. The wrapper then restores bank/status and returns
with RTL. This is distinct from the room-state setup and main callbacks.
Execute the cached bank-$8F room-main word pointer when it is nonzero.
Set X to zero for the indexed indirect JSR, and restore the caller's data bank
after the callback's RTS. Unlike setup/door wrappers, this entry has no PHP/PLP
or register-width setup; it relies on the calling gameplay path's register mode.
Prepare enemy graphics/palettes and clear the base runtime enemy records before
Initialise_Enemies fills population slots and calls Init AI. The enemy set and
population are separate resources. Reset room-level enemy hooks and bookkeeping,
process the set and load tile data into RAM, then clear inherited sprite objects.
Door transitions have already loaded enemy VRAM graphics on an earlier path.
Zero $0800 bytes of base enemy records: each word write advances X twice and
decrements the byte counter twice. Then inspect the first population ID.
An immediate $FFFF skips enemy-set processing; a nonempty population processes
the graphics/palette set before returning. This does not call enemy Init AI.
Enter with word-sized registers. First clear $1400 words ($2800 bytes) from
EnemyTileData at $7E:7000 through $7E:97FF, then reset projectile bookkeeping.
For each $10-byte population record, fill a $40-byte runtime slot from header
defaults and placement fields, expose the slot in EnemyIndex and call Init AI.
The generic init word at population offset $06 first occupies Enemy.instList;
some Init AI, including Zoomer, reads it as flags rather than an address.
The AI can change these fields. After it returns, reset/select the placeholder
spritemap, advance both cursors and stop at $FFFF. Only the nonempty-list tail
records FirstFreeEnemyIndex, the listed count and the terminator's kill byte.
The earlier JSL supplied the long return frame for Init AI's RTL. Select the
AI data bank with the swapped-word push and two bank pulls, then tail-jump
through EnemyAIPointer. The caller restores its saved bank and X/Y cursors.
Match the population's enemy ID against four-byte enemy-set entries. Prior
entries contribute tile counts from their header size divided by $20. A match
supplies the palette index and accumulated graphics offset for the runtime
slot and its spawn-data mirror. A missing match uses offset zero and $0A00
palette attributes. Population position/parameters are not graphics metadata.
Prepare destination graphics and objects, executing PLMs/door/setup ASM before
loading and initialising enemies. The room-main callback is not invoked here.
This phase can wait inside one call: IRQ handles the pending FX transfer and
door scrolling, and their flags release the two busy loops. After scrolling,
run PLMs and explicitly wait for NMI before selecting the next transition phase.
PLMs run after the final scroll update; see the visibility caveat below.
Do not return to state $0B while waiting here. IRQ scrolling continues to run
and sets bit 15 on completion. Only then restore scrolling HDMA, process PLMs
and wait for NMI. These IRQ-driven waits are not the WaitForNMI request handshake.

lines.comment: X selects this enemy's slot in the enemy arrays.
Read the population's initialisation value; it is not a script pointer yet.
Keep the starting orientation: upside right, left, down, or up (0..3).
Each orientation pointer is a word, so double the orientation number.
Y now holds the byte offset into the orientation table.
Fetch the bank-$A3 instruction list for this starting orientation.
Replace the initialisation value with the live animation-script pointer.
Select the empty spritemap until the animation supplies a frame.
Start with no visible sprite for this enemy.
A timer of one makes the script run on its next instruction update.
Schedule the orientation script's first command.
Use the local RTL as an idle handler until the script chooses movement.
Main AI can safely dispatch before the first scripted frame.
Population parameter 1 selects the crawling-speed entry.
$00FF is the sentinel for skipping the speed-table lookup.
Skip only the speed lookup; property-based sign selection still follows.
Speed entries are words; convert the selector to a byte offset.
Y indexes the selected speed word.
Load the signed 8.8 crawling speed, in pixels per frame.
Give X the chosen speed before applying direction signs.
Start Y with the same speed before applying direction signs.
Direction signs come from properties, not the initialisation value.
Isolate the two property bits that control the initial signs.
Only property value 0 takes the X-negation path.
Read the X velocity to reverse.
Complement all bits as the first step of signed negation.
Add one to finish the two's-complement negation.
Store the reversed X direction.
Initialisation is complete; this path leaves Y unchanged.
Property value 2 requests a Y reversal instead.
Values 1 and 3 leave both velocity signs unchanged.
Read the Y velocity to reverse.
Complement the Y velocity before adding one.
Complete -YVelocity without changing its 8.8 scale.
Store the reversed Y direction.
Return to the caller; this also serves as the temporary idle handler.
Read the script's next word: a bank-$A3 movement-handler address.
Install that handler for this enemy's main AI.
Advance past the handler pointer's low byte.
Advance past its high byte to the next script word.
Return the updated script pointer in Y to the instruction interpreter.
Select this enemy's state before dispatching its movement handler.
Tail-jump within bank $A3; the handler's RTL returns to the AI caller.
Read the fractional word of the separate 16.16 falling velocity.
Supply the movement helper's fractional Y distance.
Read the signed integer word of falling velocity.
Complete the helper's signed 16.16 distance at $14.$12.
Move using the current falling velocity before applying gravity.
Carry clear means unobstructed travel; continue falling.
Check whether this enemy skipped the normal speed lookup.
The $00FF sentinel has special landing-speed handling.
Ordinary speed selectors keep their existing crawling velocities.
The sentinel case resumes with +0.5 pixels per frame in 8.8.
Give X the sentinel's post-landing crawling speed.
Give Y the same positive post-landing speed.
Reset the fall state after collision.
Clear the fractional falling velocity.
Clear the integer falling velocity.
Contact ends the run of unsupported corner turns.
Recover the crawling handler saved when falling began.
Resume that handler on the next main-AI dispatch.
Finish this landing update without another movement step.
Test the integer part before adding acceleration.
Stop accelerating once the integer part is at least four.
Skip acceleration; this does not clamp an existing overshoot.
Begin acceleration with the fractional word.
Start the fractional addition without an incoming carry.
Add 0.5 px/frame per update in NTSC, or 0.625 in PAL.
Keep the new fraction; STA preserves the carry for the next ADC.
Load the integer word without disturbing that carry.
Carry any fractional overflow into the integer velocity.
Save the complete accelerated falling velocity.
Test both words for an exactly zero fall velocity.
A nonzero fraction keeps the falling handler active.
The fraction was zero; check the integer word too.
A nonzero integer likewise keeps falling active.
Zero velocity selects the vertical-crawling handler.
Install it for the next dispatch, not a second move this update.
Return from this falling-AI update.
Check for the specific earthquake update that makes crawlers let go.
The falling transition triggers when the quake timer is $001E.
Other timer values proceed with ordinary wall crawling.
Check the earthquake type as well as its timer.
Only quake type $0014 triggers this detachment path.
Other earthquake types do not detach this crawler here.
Remember the crawling handler to resume after a landing.
Save the bank-local return-to-crawling handler.
Select the separate falling state.
Schedule falling, but continue this invocation's crawl step.
Clear the fractional distance word at $12/$13.
Start the integer word at $14/$15 with a zero sign extension.
X velocity presses into the wall while Y travels along it.
A nonnegative speed needs no negative sign extension.
Negative speed needs an all-ones integer sign extension.
Write 8.8 speed across $13/$14 to form 16.16 distance at $14.$12.
Adjust the integer part for an extra pixel toward the wall.
Nonnegative X presses one pixel farther to the right.
Negative X presses one pixel farther to the left.
The negative support-probe distance is ready.
Add one pixel in the positive X direction.
Keep the extra probe pixel in the integer distance word.
Probe wall contact with X velocity plus the extra pixel.
Carry clear means no wall was found: try an outside corner.
Wall contact breaks the streak of unsupported corner turns.
Reset the shared turn counter before travelling along the wall.
Align Y to any applicable non-square slope before Y travel.
Begin a fresh fractional word for travel along the wall.
Begin with a zero integer sign extension.
Use the stored Y speed for the actual along-wall movement.
Nonnegative Y does not need an all-ones sign extension.
Sign-extend an upward, negative Y speed.
Expand signed 8.8 Y speed into the helper's 16.16 distance.
